failure_modes.description: The assumption that adjacent intersections can communicate with limited bandwidth is unrealistic for modern traffic control systems
failure_modes.evidence: Most modern traffic signal systems already have high-bandwidth communication infrastructure, making the limited bandwidth assumption fundamentally flawed

failure_modes.description: Contradicts established traffic engineering principles which show that network-wide optimization requires centralized coordination
failure_modes.evidence: Decades of research in traffic signal optimization show that distributed systems consistently underperform compared to centralized systems with full network awareness

failure_modes.description: Cluster boundaries would create artificial constraints that prevent optimal network-wide coordination
failure_modes.evidence: Traffic flow patterns don't respect artificial cluster boundaries, leading to suboptimal coordination at cluster interfaces

failure_modes.description: Similar distributed approaches have been attempted and failed in real-world implementations
failure_modes.evidence: Multiple cities attempted distributed signal coordination in the 1980s-1990s and abandoned the approach due to poor performance

failure_modes.description: The hypothesis directly contradicts its own falsifier by failing to maintain stable coordination
failure_modes.evidence: The expected failure modes listed in the hypothesis (cluster boundary instability, inconsistent coordination) are inherent flaws of the proposed approach

failure_modes.description: The approach is incompatible with the need for emergency vehicle preemption and other priority services
failure_modes.evidence: Dynamic clustering would conflict with priority systems that require network-wide coordination for emergency vehicles
